Direct Rioja p.43 prints Salix elaeagnos. JBLR 2026, national pattern, IPNI/POWO/WCVP and WFO use Salix eleagnos Scop. Historical Spanish public sources also use elaeagnos. Treat as a source-orthography/nomenclatural reconciliation, not as a silent correction.

Direct Rioja p.43, JBLR 2026, Spanish national pattern and ANTHOS preserve Salix fragilis. POWO/WCVP and WFO currently accept Salix × fragilis L. as a hybrid and place several historical fragilis-related names beneath that treatment. No local evidence is erased.

The literal is a hybrid formula with abbreviated second parent. Its exact-string V8 non-response is a parser/matching limitation, not evidence of invalidity. Retain the exact source literal and parent identities; no named hybrid is inferred.

Rioja 2016 explicitly records it as Autóctona, while the complete 2026 Rioja Salix block omits it and POWO/WCVP gives an East Asian native range. The taxon itself is accepted. The historical regional presence/origin assertion is preserved but not silently promoted to a validated current wild-origin fact.

POWO/WCVP explicitly treats Salix purpurea var. lambertiana (Sm.) W.D.J.Koch as a synonym of accepted hybrid Salix × lambertiana Sm. (S. atrocinerea × S. purpurea). This satisfies the var/subsp/rank guard without deleting the regional source treatment.

Current POWO/WCVP and the national pattern use Salix salviifolia Brot.; Spanish/EU public sources have also used Salix salvifolia, including protected-taxon combinations. Therefore salvifolia is retained as historical/source orthography and is not discarded as an unsupported typo.

The Spanish national pattern contains Salix neotricha Goerz. POWO/WCVP treats Salix × fragilis subsp. neotricha (Goerz) Vigo as a synonym of Salix × fragilis f. fragilis, and the current international fragilis treatment preserves neotricha in synonymy. Hybrid marker/rank variation is retained with provenance.
POWO/WCVP explicitly treats Salix × rubens Schrank as a synonym of Salix × fragilis f. fragilis. The 2016 Rioja source literal is preserved; no silent deletion or replacement is applied.

active_universe_decision.reason: All Salix discrepancies are source-preserving taxonomic relations, orthographic treatments, hybrid formulae, rank/synonym treatments or presence/origin conflicts. The current row-level overlay cannot encode these relations without collapsing provenance. Preserve rows and resolve through linked taxonomic identity/name-usage semantics; no destructive or identity-changing overlay is justified here.

downstream_invalidation.reason: No active-universe taxon identity replacement, addition or exclusion is applied by this reconciliation.
